tagline: From Lincoln's birthplace through the knobs to Federal Hill.
intro: US 31E sets out from the farm where Abraham Lincoln was born and runs northeast through the Kentucky knobs to Bardstown, about 28 miles. It keeps to the line of the old Cumberland Trail, beside which Thomas Lincoln leased the Knob Creek farm in hopes of getting back the one his son was born on.

Hodgenville grew up around a mill Robert Hodgen built on the North Fork of the Nolin River in 1789, and its square holds two bronze Lincolns, one a boy and one a man. Farther on, Athertonville distilled whiskey beside Knob Creek until a fire in 1972. LaRue County had voted itself dry decades before.

moments.title: Sinking Spring Farm
moments.text: Up 56 steps, one for each year of Lincoln's life, a 1911 memorial hall keeps a stand-in for his birth cabin, built of logs dating mostly from the 1840s.

moments.title: Knob Creek Farm
moments.text: Lincoln lived here from two to seven and nearly drowned in the swollen creek, until his friend and neighbor Austin Gollaher held out a branch.

moments.title: Federal Hill
moments.text: Senator John Rowan's brick mansion in Bardstown, where Lafayette and Henry Clay came calling, took the name of Stephen Foster's song when the state made it a park in 1923.
